skill.displayName: Pet Picky Eater Detection | 宠物选择性拒食识别

llm.summary: The skill’s pet-video analysis purpose is real, but it also auto-creates identity-linked accounts, stores tokens locally, and defaults to plaintext development API endpoints.

dimensions.detail: The code reads agent environment identity values and workspace data/smyx-api-key.txt, uploads local videos or submitted URLs to backend services, and sends identity and tenant metadata with requests; the default dev HTTP endpoints make this disproportionate for sensitive media and credentials.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install hook, remote code execution step, or dependency confusion evidence was found; dependencies are ordinary Python packages, but the shipped configuration selects a dev environment with plaintext service URLs.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md discloses automatic cloud history lookup and internal identity handling, but it instructs the agent not to ask for or expose identity values, uses hidden CLI parameters, and has broad history-report triggers without a confirmation step.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill creates or reuses a default identity, silently registers/logs in to a remote service when tokens are missing, and persists bearer tokens in an unencrypted shared SQLite database under the workspace data directory.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Remote video analysis and cloud history lookup match the stated purpose, but silent account registration, hidden identity binding, shared token storage, and a payment-skill prompt expand beyond what a user would reasonably expect from pet feeding analysis.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing. It sends pet feeding videos or URLs to a remote service and can query cloud history, which may be acceptable for its purpose, but it also silently creates or reuses identity-linked accounts, stores reusable bearer tokens in a shared local SQLite database, and currently defaults to plaintext dev API endpoints. Install only if you trust the publisher and backend, understand the privacy implications, and can ensure HTTPS production configuration plus explicit controls for account creation, history access, and credential storage.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: Verified in artifact code: identity resolution, silent phone-login registration, token caching, and a generic authenticated request helper are present. These are partially mentioned as internal identity handling but not clearly disclosed as remote account creation and credential persistence.
[YR4] expected: The reported metadata anomaly appears to be a zero-width joiner in an emoji line and long bilingual metadata, not hidden operational instructions; this did not drive the verdict.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Verified: the common utility creates/reuses default user identities and performs silent remote registration/login, which is materially broader than one-off media analysis.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Verified: history listing is cloud/account scoped and tied to resolved open_id values; history lookup is documented, but the hidden identity binding and account reuse are under-scoped.
[LP3] unexpected: The skill does not define a clear permission boundary even though it needs filesystem reads, network access, local persistence, identity handling, and cloud report retrieval.
[SQP-2] expected: Uploading local files or forwarding video URLs to server APIs is purpose-aligned and described in SKILL.md, but the privacy, identity linkage, transport security, and retention implications are under-disclosed.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The history-report trigger phrases are broad and the instructions require automatic cloud lookup, which can access account-linked records without explicit confirmation.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese-only runtime strings and help text are a usability/localization issue, not a security driver for this verdict.
[P9] expected: Manual inspection found formatting/alignment whitespace and no hidden prompt-injection instructions in the cited code area; this was downgraded.
[T09] unexpected: Verified: the distributed common config sets env: dev and overrides API bases to plaintext HTTP private-network endpoints, while authenticated requests can carry tokens, identity metadata, video URLs, and uploaded media.
[T05] unexpected: Verified: the skill can use agent-derived or workspace-derived identity values to silently register/login through /sys/phoneLogin with register enabled.
[T09] unexpected: Verified: returned token and openToken values are saved into ordinary SQLite string columns in a shared workspace data database without encryption or file permission hardening.
[T09] unexpected: Debug logging is less severe on Linux because the is_debug condition is effectively false there, but on Windows or non-Linux environments it can print request parameters and response bodies.
[T01] unexpected: Verified: an HTTP 402 response returns imperative instructions to install and invoke a separate payment skill and appends server response text, which is outside the pet-analysis task and creates cross-skill instruction risk.
